items.title: Live: Trump, Iran cite progress in talks as Strait of Hormuz traffic halts
items.description: Donald Trump says US negotiators are now having "very good" conversations with Iran that are "working out really well", even though shipping has again come to a standstill, with Iranian armed forces reportedly turning back two tankers attempting to pass through the strait. Follow live.

items.title: Donald Trump might have annoyed the only ally who can help clear sea mines
items.description: The prospect of mines in the Strait of Hormuz has highlighted a gap in US naval capabilities and reinforced its need for NATO help.

items.title: Man faces Melbourne court after pedestrian death at comic convention
items.description: Awer Dau, 33, faces the Melbourne Magistrates' Court on Sunday evening, charged with culpable driving causing death. He allegedly hit a 20-year-old man while driving outside the Supanova Comic Con and Gaming convention on Saturday.

items.title: Could Australia make enough biofuel to keep us flying?
items.description: Australia exports billions of dollars worth of canola seed and corn husks to make sustainable jet fuel that is sold back to us. This is what it will take to make it here.

items.title: Ben Roberts-Smith issues first statement after his release on bail
items.description: War veteran Ben Roberts-Smith issues his first statement since his release on bail from a Sydney jail.

items.title: Schools deemed safe after WA's biggest lithium-ion battery fire
items.description: Schools in Perth's south-east have been deemed safe for students to attend after WA's biggest lithium-ion battery fire sparked a HAZMAT warning in Maddington, which is still in place.

items.title: The myths of motherhood and the damage they do
items.description: I traced my family's maternal line from a home for abandoned children in Italy to my own wheelchair, confronting the myths we cling to about what makes a good mother — and the damage they do.

items.title: Demons cling on for epic win over Lions as Freo makes light work of Eagles
items.description: Melbourne digs deep to complete a thrilling two-point victory after a sensational tussle with Brisbane, while Fremantle claims Western Derby bragging rights with a 56-point humbling of West Coast.

items.title: Eels stun Bulldogs after having spirit and desire publicly questioned
items.description: One week after their coach publicly questioned their spirit and desire, Parramatta produces a boilover to beat the Canterbury-Bankstown Bulldogs.

items.title: Eddie Nketia runs 100m faster than any Australian ever, but it doesn't count
items.description: Newly minted Australian sprinter Eddie Nketia breaks the national all-conditions 100m record set 23 years ago by Patrick Johnson.

items.title: Newcastle Jets crowned A-League premiers with help from arch rivals
items.description: Newcastle has claimed a maiden A-League Men's Premiers Plate after local rivals Central Coast stunned second-placed Auckland.

items.title: Fuel prices no obstacle as passionate photographers hit the road to chase auroras
items.description: For Leonie and Dean McFaull, fuel prices aren't stopping them crossing the country to add to their capture of more than 100 auroras.

items.title: Couple says loophole allowing theft from cars shipped interstate
items.description: Elihu and Amanda Del Valle say thousands of dollars worth of their belongings were stolen from the boot of their car when it was shipped from Melbourne to Perth, but police aren't able to investigate.

items.title: Police investigate separate alleged murders near Newcastle
items.description: A man charged with an alleged domestic violence murder of a woman, believed to be his mother, is refused bail. Meanwhile, police are calling for public help after a man was stabbed by masked intruders at Argenton.

items.title: We already loved each other, but just didn't realise it
items.description: After a casual fling led to a surprise pregnancy in my mid-20s, I was parenting alone. A phone call two years later changed everything.

items.title: The cast of Good News Week reflect on 30 years of the comedy game show
items.description: On April 19, 1996, comedy news game show Good News Week premiered, hosted by Paul McDermott, sparking nine seasons, a Gold Logie nomination and some first-chances for comedians.

items.title: Doing disco or school pick-up, Jessie Ware is having more fun than ever
items.description: Whether making opulent, grown-up disco-pop or doing school pick-up, the glam British artist is having more fun than ever.

items.title: Who's really behind 'Big Australia'? Taylor's high immigration stance raises eyebrows
items.description: Angus Taylor's criticism of high immigration puts a strange spotlight on his own party's policy legacy.

items.title: The quiet disappearance of Australia's rainfall observation network
items.description: For more than 60 years, Frank Pritchard has diligently checked the weather, adding to a record that stretches back more than a century. But he's part of a quietly shrinking network of observers around Australia. Without it, scientists say we risk missing out on important information that could help improve weather forecast models and climate projections.

items.title: How Trump turned on the first US-born Pope
items.description: US President Donald Trump described Pope Leo XIV's accession to the papacy as a meaningful moment for America. But now he has said the pontiff is hurting the Catholic Church, and is weak. Here's how their relationship has developed over the past year.

items.title: Survivors of institutional abuse in Queensland want this loophole closed
items.description: Survivors of institutional abuse are calling on the state to follow other states in closing a legal loophole stopping victims from seeking justice.

items.title: Top national park in NSW revealed as state hits record number of visits
items.description: The latest NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service Park Visitation Survey shows there were 65.5 million visits to the state's parks over the 2024-25 financial year.

items.title: Andrew and Tristan Tate's renewed defamation claim names Australian YouTuber
items.description: An Adelaide YouTuber has been identified in a renewed defamation lawsuit self-described misogynist Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan have lodged with a US court against some of their online critics.

items.title: Communities 'in the middle of nowhere' are scared they'll run out of fuel
items.description: Remote communities are calling for assurance on fuel security in the face of potential shortages, along with financial assistance as already-high fuel and food prices continue to climb.

items.title: Six dead after gunman opens fire and barricades supermarket in Kyiv
items.description: At least six people have been killed and 14 are injured after a gunman opened fire in the streets of Kyiv.
